sentences.text: 1 Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the present applicant has been falsely implicated and he has not committed any offence as alleged.

Attention has been drawn towards the impugned First Information Report where the date of incident has been indicated as 3rd January 2024, but the First Information Report was lodged on 02.02.2024 and the reason of delay has not been explained properly.
In the aforesaid First Information Report, the allegations have been levelled against the present applicant and one another person.
The learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that pursuant to the direction being issued by this court, the prosecutrix has been examined by the learned trial court.

Statement of the expert witness, i.e., Dr Priyanka, Medical Officer, CSC,
Akhbarpur has been recorded.
The learned counsel for the applicant has drawn attention of this Court towards the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161 and 164 CrPC.

In the First Information Report, it has been indicated that on the basis of telephonic call of one accused person to the effect that he is having some photos of the victim which would be circulated if she does not come to meet him and she went to one place at Banpurva Forest at 6:30 AM on 30th January 2024, where both the accused persons met her and committed rape.
One accused was carrying a pistol with him and has threatened the victim.

In her statement recorded under Section 161 CrPC,
she changed the story and has stated that on fateful day at 6:30 AM, she went to the jungle to ease out where both the accused persons were present.
They clicked the naked photographs of the victim and threatened that they will circulate those photographs and on such threat they committed rape.

In her statement recorded under Section 164 CrPC, she again changed the statement to the effect that both the accused persons compelled the victim to put off her clothes, thereafter they clicked the naked photographs of the victim and later on committed rape.

However, while recording her evidence before the trial court and during cross-examination, she again change the story and has submitted that she had not gone to ease out in the jungle as there is toilet in her residence, but she had gone to jungle for the purpose of morning walk along with both the accused persons and both the accused persons committed rape with her after clicking the naked photographs.
In her cross examination, she change the story and has stated that no naked photographs were clicked by the accused persons and she had not apprised this fact to the police or to the court.
She has also stated that since no photos were clicked, therefore the photos were not circulated.
In her statement, the expert witness, i.e., the Doctor has also stated that in her medical examination, there was no symptoms of physical assault on the body of the victim.
The learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the victim has changed the allegations at every stage and there is no consistency in her statement.
Even expert witness, i.e., Doctor has not verified the factum of rape.
The present applicant is having no prior criminal history of any kind whatsoever.
He is a young person and has been falsely implicated.
Therefore, if he is enlarged on bail, he shall shall cooperate in the trial proceedings and shall not misuse the liberty of bail.
Further, the applicant shall abide by all terms and conditions of the bail order, the applicant may be enlarged on bail.
The learned AGA has opposed the bail application by submitting that the victim has however change the story at various stages, but so far as the allegation of rape is concerned, that is intact.

On being confronted on the point of that since the relevant witnesses, i.e., the prosecutrix and the expert witness, the Doctor have already been examined, the learner AGA has submitted that though those witnesses have been examined but there are still prosecution witnesses which are to be examined.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, perusing the material available on record,
arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, I find it a fit case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant-Sachin Yadav, be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicants fail to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation,
then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law,
under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
(v) Before parting with, it is expected that the trial shall be concluded with expedition, strictly in accordance with law, without adjourning the case for any unnecessary reason.

Further, the learned trial court may take all coercive measures,
as per law, if either of the parties do not co-operate in the trial properly.
